Ravi — thanks, this is perfect detail to start with. High-level answers up front then a short action plan below.

High level:
- Split by workload: 3 node pools (control/system, inference edge, batch). Keep inference nodes focused on low-latency CPU+GPU configs and tune for low tail latency.
- KV cache: local NVMe is ideal for per-node KV/cache hot paths (fast, avoids network hops). Use a replicated persistent store (Ceph) for model artifacts, checkpoints, and indexed state.
- Network: MTU/jumbo frames help only if your switching fabric supports it consistently end-to-end; we recommend testing baseline first. Prioritize separate VLANs for inter-pod traffic, storage (Ceph/iSCSI), and management.

Ravi/Soojin — quick recommendations based on the profile you sent:

Node pools (suggested):
- system-control (3 masters -> k8s control plane on dedicated VMs/racks; small footprint: 4 vCPU / 16GB, high-availability across racks)
- inference-cpu (6-8 nodes initially): 32 vCPU / 256GB, 2x1TB NVMe for KV cache; pod density tuned to keep tail latency low.
- inference-gpu (2-4 nodes): 8 vCPU / 64GB + 1 GPU (A100 or A10x), NVMe for local KV cache and model shards; use a label selector so the scheduler pins high-priority requests here.
- batch (2 nodes): 16 vCPU / 128GB, no GPUs required; used for nightly embedding jobs with autoscale to zero outside windows.

Storage mapping:
- Local NVMe (fast) -> ephemeral/cache PVCs via local-volume CSI. Ideal for per-node KV cache and model shard caches.
- Ceph RBD via CSI -> durable model artifacts, checkpoints, and any state that must survive node failures. Configure replication factor >= 3.
- NetApp NFS -> optional for legacy apps; avoid for high-throughput KV cache.

Network considerations:
- MTU 9000 recommended if all switches and NICs support it; otherwise stick to 1500.
- Dedicated VLANs: pod-traffic, storage, mgmt. Prefer separate physical NICs for storage traffic where possible.
- BGP-based routing or static with careful AS path planning — we'll keep load-balancer placement simple for POC.

I'll add recommended kubelet eviction thresholds, kube-reserved and system-reserved numbers in the runbook.

Couple of implementation notes / gotchas we hit on similar on-prem setups:

1) Local NVMe as KV cache
- Use a local-volume CSI driver with pod-affinity to keep cache pods on same host. Beware of eviction; ensure persistent model artifacts are on Ceph so losing a node doesn't require re-pulling large models during peak.

2) Ceph specifics
- Expose Ceph via RBD/CSI for block-level PVs. Avoid NFS for any low-latency requirements. Set rbd cache to off on clients if you have local NVMe caching to avoid double-caching issues.

3) Volume topology and scheduling
- Define two StorageClasses: fast-local (local NVMe, volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer) and durable-ceph (replicated RBD with encrypted volumes). Annotate node labels for scheduling preferences.

4) Kubelet and OS tuning
- Set kube-reserved and system-reserved based on node size (example: kube-reserved: cpu=500m,memory=1Gi for inference-cpu nodes).
- Disable swap, tune vm.swappiness=10, confirm NUMA alignment for GPUs. HugePages not required for now but useful for memory-heavy model shards.
